text_blocks.snippet: A duodenal ulcer, a sore on the lining of the duodenum (the first part of the small intestine), can cause a range of symptoms, with pain being the most common. This pain is typically a burning or gnawing sensation in the upper abdomen, which may improve with eating or worsen on an empty stomach. Other symptoms include bloating, feeling full, heartburn, indigestion, nausea, and vomiting, sometimes with blood. Weight loss and decreased appetite can also occur.
